description:
Core odds query. Returns a flat array of book prices, narrowed by any combination of event_id, player_id, team_id, sportsbook, market, league and scope. Called with no filters it paginates hard — narrow to at least one entity. Paginate with cursor.

FUTURES live here: pass scope=season for season-long futures (division/conference/championship winners, award odds, team win totals, season leaders, full-season player props — a PLAYER_TOTAL_PASS_YARDS at scope=season is a ~3,750.5 SEASON line, not a game line), or scope=tournament for golf/tennis outrights. Futures rows are described by three ORTHOGONAL axes: `marketScope` (SEASON | TOURNAMENT — the anchor the market hangs off; omitted entirely on ordinary game rows), `period` (the window within that anchor: REG_SEASON settles at the end of the regular season, FULL runs through the playoffs) and `segment` (the slice of the competition: AFC_EAST, NFC_WEST, AL, NL, SEC ... — present only when the market is segment-scoped). READ `segment` — it is load-bearing: all 32 NFL DIVISION_WINNER selections share ONE season-anchor eventId, so ignoring segment turns 8 separate division races into one nonsensical 32-team market.

Futures gotchas: winner/award markets are CATEGORICAL — one YES selection per competitor with teamSide "NONE", and most books offer no NO side, so these are not two-way markets. `eventStartTime` on a futures row is the SEASON-ANCHOR / settlement date (e.g. the Super Bowl date), NOT a kickoff. Every book's futures for a competition converge on the same season eventId, so scope=season + league is already a cross-book board. Futures are deliberately EXCLUDED from get_edges and get_arbitrage — season markets never enter de-vig or edge math (a product decision, not a gap).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor. Pass the `nextCursor` from a previous response to fetch the next page.

event_id.description: Scope to one event (UUID from list_events).

limit.description: Max rows to return (page size). Default 50, server caps apply.

market.description: Market FAMILY filter, matched as a substring (e.g. MONEYLINE, SPREAD, PLAYER_TOTAL, TEAM_TOTAL, CATEGORICAL). The specific token — DIVISION_WINNER, AWARD_MVP, SEASON_LEADER_PASS_YARDS, TEAM_TOTAL_WINS — is each row's `marketSubtype`, not this filter: winner/award futures live under market=CATEGORICAL. See list_markets.

player_id.description: Scope to one player (UUID from list_players).

scope.description: Which KIND of market to return. `event` = single-game markets. `season` = season-long futures (division/conference/championship winners, awards, team win totals, season leaders, full-season player props). `tournament` = golf/tennis tournament outrights — a different product from season futures. Exact match: `season` does NOT include TOURNAMENT rows. Omit for all scopes (the default). An unrecognised value returns 400 listing the valid ones, so a typo can never look like "no futures exist".

sportsbook.description: Sportsbook / DFS source id (e.g. draftkings, prizepicks). See list_sportsbooks.

team_id.description: Scope to one team (UUID from list_teams).

name: get_odds
